title: StarPulse machine definition
description: A lifecycle machine declared under .starpulse/machines/. Guards are field matches on the triggering event or the name of a guard an adapter registers in Python; config holds no expressions or code.

source.description: The third party that moves this machine, such as GitHub. Only that party's events move it; StarPulse observes, and the page draws the machine apart from one StarPulse's own actors move.

migrations.description: Old State to the State its live Tasks move to when this version replaces one that had the old State. A change that drops or renames a State holding live Tasks is accepted only with the mapping.

bindings.description: Adapter event name to the machine event it moves.

writers.description: Per machine event, who fires it: a bare actor (an agent, an operator) or a workflow as <instance>/<workflow>, with the trigger it fires through.

cues.description: The workflows a machine event cues, each with how its failure resolves.

tiers.description: The state ids the Star Map draws at each stage, left to right; a tier's states stack in its cell.

main_line.description: The state ids along the machine's axis, in order. A Board file without one draws its lanes in order.

rests.description: States drawn as where a lifecycle ends though the machine does not declare them final, because an event leaves them.

submachines.description: Machines that open under one of this machine's states, each a sibling file named by its stem.

next.description: The edge a finished skill hands to: the skill or operation that runs next. Absent means no edge is declared.

launches.description: Per launching workflow (its own name, or <instance>/<workflow>), the skill it starts and the sibling machine that skill draws.

label.description: The name a person reads for this state (In Progress, Needs attention); the state id when absent.

role.description: What this state is for, so StarPulse code reads the role and never the state's name: resting (a task rests here), waiting_on_fact (it leaves when a fact holds) waiting_on_person (it leaves when a person acts) or proposed (a task waits here off the lanes, never admitted, until it is promoted to the state waiting on criteria_unmet or dropped to a final state). A state flagged initial or final has that role already.

waits.description: The facts this state waits on, each a fact kind (pr_terminal, pr_merged, pr_merged_planned, pr_merged_unfinished, pr_ready, pr_red, pr_pending, deps_done, deps_unresolved, criteria_met, criteria_unmet) mapped to the event that leaves this state when the fact holds. The loader refuses an unknown fact kind and an event that is not a transition out of this state.

cite.description: The sentence of a skill that sends a session down this transition, drawn as the edge's tooltip.

actor.description: A bare actor name, or a workflow as <instance>/<workflow> naming a workflow a configured runs adapter lists.

exits.description: Per final state of the inner machine, the event of this machine that leaves the state.

routes.description: Per phase state that may follow this one in a task type's `[sequences]` entry, the event of this machine that leaves the state toward it instead of the exit's own.

when.description: What has to hold for the inner machine to run under the state.

machine.description: The sibling machine file's stem; absent when the skill has no machine.

on.description: What the page says cues it, such as a push to main.

resolves.description: forced: a failed run stays pinned until a forced rerun. next: it clears on the next run of the DAG.

grace.description: Seconds after the event a run of the DAG may take to start before the page draws it overdue. Default 300.

registered.description: The name of a guard or action an adapter registers in Python.

when.description: Every listed field of the triggering event must match.
